section_1.title: Introduction: Why Do We Model Outbreaks?
section_1.content: A brief overview of how epidemics spread in populations. Define the core objective: Predicting the 'peak' of infections and the impact of intervention.
section_1.example: A campfire analogy: One spark (infected) hits a dry forest (susceptible), quickly turning into a wildfire (epidemic) before running out of fuel (recovered/immune).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Population Dynamics & Rates
section_2.content: Establish the concept of flow. Introduce the idea that individuals transition between states at specific rates (represented as arrows in a flow diagram).
section_2.example: A faucet filling a bucket: The rate of flow determines how fast the level changes. Here, 'flow' = number of people changing status per day.

section_3.title: The SIR Framework: Defining the States
section_3.content: Visual breakdown of the three compartments: S (Susceptible), I (Infected), and R (Recovered/Removed). Use a color-coded diagram (Green -> Red -> Blue).
section_3.example: A game of Tag: Children who haven't been tagged (S), those currently 'It' (I), and those sitting out on the bench because they've already played (R).

section_4.title: Mathematical Mechanics: The Transition Equations
section_4.content: Explain the logic of transmission (S+I interaction) and recovery (I -> R). Visualize this using a graph: 'Infection Rate' curve vs. 'Recovery Rate' curve.
section_4.example: An animated bar chart showing the S-bar shrinking, the I-bar spiking, and the R-bar steadily growing over a 30-day timeline.

section_5.title: Simulation & Application: 'Flattening the Curve'
section_5.content: Show how changing transmission variables (e.g., social distancing) flattens the peak of the 'I' curve. Summarize the model's predictive power for public health policy.
section_5.example: Simulating a scenario where a digital population of robots reduces their contact rate, showing the Red 'Infection' peak drop significantly on the graph.

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject
